name: Archetype of Courage
oracle_text:
Creatures you control have first strike.
Creatures your opponents control lose first strike and can't have or gain first strike.
blocked_sentences: Creatures your opponents control lose first strike and can't have or gain first strike.

needs.what: a static effect that REMOVES one named keyword from every permanent matching its `affects` filter, and keeps it off -- the Archetype cycle's "lose <keyword> and can't have or gain <keyword>" half. It has to beat later grants, not merely subtract once: a creature the opponent later enchants with a first-strike anthem, or that enters with a first_strike keyword counter, must still not have it. Shape: `{"kind": "static", "effect": "lose_keyword", "keywords": ["first_strike"], "affects": {"types": ["Creature"], "controller": "opponent"}}`, applied after every keyword-adding step in the characteristics pipeline (and after the keyword-counter step) so that nothing can add the keyword back.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `grant_keyword` is the only keyword static in `static_effects` and it is additive-only: `characteristics.py` builds a creature's keyword set by `keywords.update(...)` over every matching `grant_keyword` and every keyword counter, and no step in that loop ever discards a keyword. The only subtractive thing in the whole list is `lose_all_abilities`, which is far too broad -- it would strip the opponents' creatures of flying, their triggered abilities and their activated abilities as well, turning a first-strike hoser into a board-wide Humility half. There is no negation flag on `grant_keyword` (`op_options` and the static reader both know only `keywords`), and `not_keywords` in `static_filter_keys` only filters who a static sees, it cannot take a keyword away.
